subject: Request: Bridge concession for SKU shipping delay (KiteHealth / DEAL-5583)
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan@kitehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SKU phase delay — need to discuss commercial make-good

Hi Monica,

Quick heads up — our product team just told us the private routing SKU that we were counting on for the enterprise rollout won’t be ready for another 6 weeks. That feature was a gating item for our customer integration and is the reason we committed to Redwood as the preferred inference provider.

This delay puts our go-live out and impacts our forecasted usage and launch marketing. Given the change, the executive team is asking for a one-time commercial accommodation to bridge the gap while you ship the capability.

High level:
- ARR: ~$250k (first 12 months) under current contract
- Impact: ~40% lower usage in month 1 post-launch
- Requested: a one-time credit of $75,000 applied to our onboarding/invoice to help absorb migration costs and extended POC effort

I've attached the current SOW and our Q2 usage snapshot. Can you escalate on your side and let me know what is possible? We need something confirmed this week so our CFO can sign off.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Director of Procurement, KiteHealth

Folks — forwarding an urgent request from KiteHealth (DEAL-5583). TL;DR: feature ship slipped ~6 weeks; customer asks for $75k credit. They are pushing for commit this week.

Deal context:
- ACV/ARR ~ $250k / year; strategic health vertical, strong reference potential
- SOW already signed; impact is on timing and initial usage (affects our 90-day ramp numbers)
- Customer willing to accept a documented remediation plan and priority support

Options I'm proposing (please comment):
1) Approve one-time invoice credit of $75k (full ask) — fast, but higher short-term revenue hit
2) Approve a $50–60k service credit applied over 3 months + priority early access and dedicated onboarding hours
3) Deny financial concession, offer extended trial + higher engineering SLAs only (risk of churn)

Asking for an exec decision by COB tomorrow (7/20) so I can share specifics with KiteHealth and lock in a path. Attaching SOW + usage + internal roadmap slice.

Attachments: KiteHealth_SOW_v4.pdf, KiteHealth_Usage_Q2.csv, Roadmap_SKU_Phase.pdf

—Monica
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: SKU phase delay — need to discuss commercial make-good

Thanks Monica — appreciate the quick escalation. A few clarifying Qs before I weigh in:
- Is this a one-time invoice credit request ($75k), or are they expecting a lasting rate concession?
- If we provide a credit, what is the net expected ROI (retention probability, expansion likelihood) — Laura, any win probability updates?

Finance/Commercial considerations (Rishi, FYI):
- One-time credit vs. percentage rebate: prefer one-time credit applied to next invoice to avoid ongoing accounting complexity
- If approved, recommend formal amendment (DocuSign) and milestone language that ties credit release to the rollout plan and support hours used

Please run scenarios: full $75k; middle $50–60k conditional; and non-financial-only. I want risk/benefit and an accounting treatment recommendation.

Vivek
VP, Commercial Strategy
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SKU phase delay — need to discuss commercial make-good

Recommend approving a conditional credit to preserve the relationship and the reference opportunity — customer looks strategic. My suggested structure:
- Concession: $60,000 one-time credit applied across the first invoice(s) as a service credit (not percentage pricing change)
- Conditions: requires (a) signed amendment documenting new ship date and acceptance criteria, (b) agreed-upon 5 SLA review checkpoints over first 90 days, and (c) a public reference agreement after GA
- Offsets: offer 20 hours of priority integration support and a 2-week dedicated onboarding window at no charge

This limits the hit, buys time for engineering to ship, and creates clear deliverables. If product can commit to earlier ship, we can consider increasing the credit by up to $10k.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Enterprise
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SKU phase delay — need to discuss commercial make-good

Adding product detail: the SKU routing fix is a cross-runtime change; current roadmap shows a planned release in ~5 weeks if we do normal QA. There is a low-likelihood fast path, but it would require pulling a lead eng and pausing another customer workstream — estimated engineering cost ~$40k in incremental contractor/time.

Given that, here's a recommended commercial + product package that I think is realistic and protects revenue:
- Offer a $50,000 credit (compromise vs $75k ask)
- Provide priority early-access build and 30 hours of senior eng support during integration window (can be scheduled within next 2 weeks)
- Commit to biweekly progress notes to the customer and a firm ship target of 5 weeks with rollback/mitigation plan

If sales wants to meet $60k, product can consider accelerating but only with a clear budget trade-off; engineering needs the go/no-go by EOD 7/21.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime

- Approve a $50,000 one-time service credit to KiteHealth (applied to first invoice)
- Include 30 hours senior eng support + priority early access build
- Legal to issue an amendment (DocuSign) with explicit milestones and credit release tied to the signed amendment

Open items / owners:
- Rishi: confirm accounting treatment and revenue reporting for one-time credit (due 7/21 EOD)
- Legal: draft amendment template and DocuSign link (suggested wording attached)
- Karthik: confirm target ship date and provide biweekly status notes to customer (first note by 7/26)
- Monica: send formal commercial offer to KiteHealth and confirm acceptance; request signature on amendment by 7/23

Susan / Tom — appreciate your patience. We can confirm the $50k credit plus the technical support outlined above. I will get the amendment over to you this morning; please let me know if you need alternate wording.

Monica Patel
